authority.legal_name: Roads and Transport Authority (RTA), Government of Dubai
authority.geography_type: coastal emirate with a tidal creek, a built water canal and an open-Gulf waterfront
authority.home_waters_label: Dubai's creek, canal and Gulf waterfront

mandate.summary: RTA plans, builds and regulates all of Dubai's public transport — metro, tram, bus, taxi and the marine network (abra, water bus, water taxi, ferry). Marine transport master-planning is an explicit, quantified part of its remit under Dubai 2040 and the Marine Transport Master Plan 2030.
current_priorities: Deliver the Marine Transport Master Plan 2030 (ridership, network length, stations, lines, fleet)
Advance the Dubai 2040 '20-minute city' with water as a feeder mode to metro/tram/bus
Renew and decarbonize the marine fleet (incl. the world's first electric 3D-printed abra) under UAE Net Zero 2050
Protect and grow the heritage abra trade while adding premium and high-value corridors

policy_targets.vision: Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan ('20-minute city'); UAE Net Zero 2050

marine_master_plan_2030.stations: 48 -> 79 marine stations (Dubai Creek, Dubai Water Canal, Arabian Gulf coastline, waterfront projects)
marine_master_plan_2030.electrification: World's first electric abra via 3D printing (-90% manufacturing time, -30% cost)

policy_targets.relevance: Every Master Plan 2030 target — more ridership, more network length, more lines, a renewed and electrified fleet — is exactly what a zero-emission foiling tier delivers. Navier is the premium, fast, near-silent edge of the renewal RTA has already committed to, and it advances Net Zero 2050.

precedent.headline: Dubai already runs one of the world's most-used public marine networks — and has a funded plan to nearly double it.

existing_marine_network.modes: Abra (heritage + electric), Water Bus, Water Taxi, Dubai Ferry
existing_marine_network.scale_2023: ~14.7M marine trips/yr across 48 stations and 7 lines on a 55 km network
existing_marine_network.recent_stations: New abra/ferry station at Souk Al Marfa (Dubai Islands / Deira Islands); marine interfaces planned into Metro Purple Line stations
existing_marine_network.note: Marine transport is already a mainstream public mode in Dubai, not a novelty. The plan is to expand it, electrify it, and add high-value lines.

uae_internal_corridor.link: Dubai <-> Abu Dhabi (and the northern emirates)
uae_internal_corridor.stat: ~140 km road corridor, heavily trafficked; no fast public water link today
uae_internal_corridor.relevance: A domestic, within-UAE marine express between the two largest emirates is national connectivity the road network can't relieve — a long-range, optional extension after the home-water network is proven.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the software-defined, zero-emission foiling upgrade to a marine mode Dubai already runs at massive scale and is committed to expanding. Foiling hulls are faster, near-silent, low-wake and far more efficient per passenger-mile than the current displacement fleet — opening premium and feeder corridors the abras and water buses can't serve, while sitting entirely above (and protecting) the heritage abra trade.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real RTA marine stations/berths during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors live RTA marine stations along the Creek, Water Canal and Gulf waterfront; extensions add real water-accessible districts named in the Master Plan 2030.

boarding_points.name: Al Seef Marine Transport Station (Dubai Creek)
Deira Old Souq / Bur Dubai abra station (Creek mouth)
Madinat Jumeirah / Burj Al Arab waterfront

domestic_pairs.rationale: Dense Marina/JBR to Palm Jumeirah; today a slow road loop around the Palm. Anchor premium corridor.
Short, high-frequency hop between Marina and Bluewaters/Ain Dubai.
Live creek corridor; foiling adds speed and zero-emission running between heritage core and Festival City.
Creek to Water Canal corridor linking the historic core with the Business Bay canal district (displacement / no-foil through the canal).
Coastal run linking the Jumeirah beachfront to the Marina/Harbour cluster, bypassing Sheikh Zayed Road.
Mina Rashid / Port Rashid waterfront to the new Dubai Islands station; coastal, bypasses Deira road congestion.
Offshore run to the World Islands; demonstrates quiet, low-wake island access conventional craft struggle to serve.
Burj Al Arab / Madinat waterfront to Dubai Harbour; coastal premium leg.
Hub-spoke: Dubai Marina ↔ Deira Old Souq / Bur Dubai abra station (Creek mouth) (orphan BP on published network)
Hub-spoke: Dubai Marina ↔ Al Jaddaf Marine Station (upper Creek) (orphan BP on published network)
Hub-spoke: Dubai Marina ↔ Dubai Water Canal — Jumeirah/Safa (orphan BP on published network)

regional_links.note: Secondary and clearly optional. The Dubai<->Abu Dhabi leg is DOMESTIC within the UAE (national connectivity), not cross-border. Cross-Gulf legs (Doha, Manama, Muscat) are explicitly out of the core proposal and belong on a far-future roadmap only.

links.note: Within-UAE express between Dubai and Abu Dhabi waterfronts; long-range (Quanta-LR class). Optional extension after the home-water network is proven.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings. Hand-curated waypoints required wherever the Palm breakwater, the creek mouth, port traffic separation, canal bridges, or offshore reclamation would otherwise be clipped.

hazards.detail: Palm Jumeirah is land/reclamation; routes to/from the Palm must round the outer crescent breakwater through the marked openings — NEVER straight across the fronds or trunk.
Marina and Dubai Harbour are enclosed by breakwaters; snap entries to the marked harbour mouths, not the breakwater rock.

hazards.hazard: Dubai Creek mouth & Port Rashid (Mina Rashid)
hazards.detail: The creek mouth is shared with commercial and abra traffic; Mina Rashid is an active cruise/commercial port. Route through the marked channel and respect port traffic separation.
The Water Canal is narrow with multiple low road/foot bridges; canal legs must be displacement / no-foil with strict wake and speed limits, following the dredged centreline through the bridge spans.
The Deira <-> Bur Dubai abra crossings are dense and protected; geofence no-foil, low-wake zones across all abra lanes.
The World is a reclaimed archipelago served by dredged channels; snap to channel entries and keep geometry clear of the shallow inter-island flats.
Any coastal run extending south must stay clear of the Jebel Ali Port traffic separation scheme and approaches.

hazards.hazard: Dubai <-> Abu Dhabi offshore (optional link only)
hazards.detail: If the domestic UAE link is routed, keep the line in open Gulf water clear of the Jebel Ali and Khalifa Port approaches and offshore oilfield exclusion zones; hand-waypoint around all reclamation.
